subject: Dedicated capacity latency shielding proposal — Zenterra
messages:
From: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@zenterra.ai>

Cc: procurement@zenterra.ai
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: latency shielding for dedicated pool — data & ask

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we discussed on the call, Zenterra is evaluating a dedicated-capacity plan but we need a tighter tail-latency and an operational carve-out for our high-frequency inference lane. Attached is a short sample of our production p99 traces for the last 72 hours (zenterra_latency_analysis.csv).

High-level asks:
- A deterministic approach to protect a set of reserved GPUs from noisy neighbors during peak windows (we call this the "shield").
- A clear credit/mitigation plan if infrequent preemption or queuing causes >200ms increase in p95 relative to baseline.
- A short timeline to validate the solution in your staging environment (we can provide a 48-hour traffic replay).

Can you outline what options Redwood can offer (config changes, policy addenda, or credits)? If helpful I can loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Chan
Head of Platform 
Zenterra AI

Attachments: zenterra_latency_analysis.csv (CSV, 2.1MB)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@zenterra.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: latency shielding for dedicated pool — data & ask

Hi Oliver — thanks for the data, that helps. Looping in Lauren (legal) and Ben (customer success / sales ops) so we can align the technical and commercial sides.

Initial thoughts from the runtime/product side:
- We can provision a dedicated "low-noise lane": a subset of reserved GPUs pinned to your tenant with stricter preemption thresholds and reduced burst eviction. This is a config on Dedicated.
- Additive options: token-level request prioritization and an inflight-headroom token pool reserved for the lane to reduce queuing.
- If latency regresses beyond agreed thresholds we propose a blended remediation: immediate mitigation (traffic shaping/fallback to warm variants) + retrospective credit calculation.

Questions for you:
1) Which windows are most critical for you (local TZ)? Do you have a daily peak or weekly batch cycles?
2) For the credit model, do you want credits tied to seconds of degraded p95 or a percentage of monthly committed spend?

Ben/Lauren — can you weigh in on whether a short SLA amendment (one-pager) + a short validation run (48h) would be sufficient from procurement/legal perspective? If so, I can draft a proposed addendum and propose a verification plan.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Inference Partnerships
Redwood Inference

----

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@zenterra.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: latency shielding for dedicated pool — data & ask

Oliver — appreciate the trace. I reviewed with infra; attaching a short draft (proposed-sla-amendment-Zenterra.pdf) that captures a practical approach. Highlights:
- Dedicated lane: 8 reserved GPUs (M-series) for initial pilot, pinned to your account during peak windows.
- Preemption policy: reduced eviction probability (90th percentile protection) for pinned workloads; non-pinned workloads are eligible for preemption first.
- Headroom credit: if p95 increases >200ms over baseline for more than 30 minutes cumulatively in a calendar month, credit = 2% of monthly committed fee per 30-minute block (capped at 25%).
- Validation: 48-hour replay, plus observability snapshot (token-level tracing + tail token sampling).

Requested actions from Zenterra:
- Confirm desired window (we can support rolling windows or daily anchored windows).
- Confirm commit level (monthly reserved node commitment) to enable the dedicated pool sizing.

Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment-Zenterra.pdf (PDF, 450KB)

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Chan <oliver.chan@zenterra.ai>

Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 07:20:00 -0700

Thanks Ben — read through the draft. A few quick notes from procurement/tech: 
- Zenterra can commit to a 6-month reserved node commitment at the pilot size, but we need a stronger uptime target for the lane during defined peak hours (we would like a 99.95% p95 availability for the shielded lane during our 09:00-21:00 UTC window).
- For credits: preference for credits expressed as a percentage of committed spend (your draft is aligned), but we need an explicit reconciliation cadence and an SLA scoreboard that we can consume via an API or shared Drive link.
- On the technical side: we want an explicit fall-through model — if the lane cannot meet latency targets, what fallback model will you serve (smaller model, cached prefix, or route to warm variant)? Please include the fallback behavior in the addendum.

We can run the 48-hour traffic replay next Thursday (UTC). Please confirm sign-off path (DocuSign / SOW) and whether any legal redlines are expected.

Oliver

- Commercial: Ben indicated procurement OK to a 6-month reserve; we will reflect 6-month commit and the credit cap in the addendum.
- Legal: Lauren flagged two small redlines around the SLA scoreboard and auditability; she suggests a short appendix describing the metrics and access (we can provide a read-only Drive folder + an API token for scoreboard export). Lauren — I left a couple of inline comments in the PDF.
